Also find relevant experimental evidence if clinical cognitive performance was not formally tested.'}

**Yes, with an important qualification.** NMDAR autoimmunity can contribute to new or worsening cognitive problems after herpes simplex encephalitis, particularly when it presents as post-HSE autoimmune encephalitis. Cognitive and behavioral changes may include memory or other thinking difficulties. But the presence of NMDAR antibodies alone does **not** establish that a person will have cognitive impairment; some antibody-positive patients do not develop a clear autoimmune syndrome. Cognitive deficits may also result from the original HSE, making the additional effect of autoimmunity difficult to separate.

The searches in this session did not return study-level results, so I cannot give a reliable quantitative estimate or claim that antibody positivity by itself predicts cognitive performance. The best-supported conclusion is that post-HSE NMDAR autoimmunity **can** affect cognition, especially in symptomatic autoimmune relapse, but its independent effect is not settled.
